_fictional: FICTIONAL RECORDINGS, HAND-WRITTEN, NEVER CAPTURED. This repository has no OPENAI_API_KEY, no GOOGLE_FACTCHECK_API_KEY and no route to either service, so nothing here was recorded from a live API. Each entry is what a plausible provider or model answer would look like for one claim of the fictional golden set — evidence for testing Re-Vera's rules, not evidence about the world, and not evidence that any real model returns these answers. Every outlet, URL, figure and quotation is invented. See eval/fixtures/README.md.

official.text: Average recreational screen time among 13 to 16 year olds rose 34 per cent between 2020 and 2025, from 2.9 to 3.9 hours a day.

judge.evidence: The Education Statistics Portal records a 34 per cent rise in teenage screen time since 2020, not 400 per cent.

web.quote: All 137 secondary schools now run the digital literacy module
web.text: All 137 secondary schools now run the digital literacy module, completing a rollout that began in 2024.

web.quote: The media literacy module reached every secondary school this term
web.text: The media literacy module reached every secondary school this term, the ministry confirmed to reporters.

judge.evidence: Island Wire and Straits Beacon both report the module running in every secondary school.

The media literacy module reached every secondary school this term

factcheck.quote: Half of students failed one identification exercise in the study
factcheck.text: Checkpoint SG rated this Partly true. Half of students failed one identification exercise in the study, but the study did not ask them whether they could tell real news from fake, and performance varied sharply by year group.

judge.evidence: Checkpoint SG found half of students failed one exercise, which is not the same as saying they cannot tell real news from fake.
cited_spans: Half of students failed one identification exercise in the study

cited.text: The spokesperson said: “The first cohort's results are below what we hoped for, which is why we are revising the module rather than dropping it.” The word reported was not used.

judge.evidence: The ministry transcript has the spokesperson describing a module being revised, not called a failure.
